The "All for Alex" softball initiative is an annual SEC-wide campaign honoring late Mississippi State player Alex Wilcox, who passed away from ovarian cancer in 2018 at age 18. Held annually, teams wear teal to raise awareness for cancer, celebrating her legacy and fighting spirit. Key Details of "All for Alex" Purpose: To honor Alex Wilcox, raise awareness for ovarian cancer, and spread the message that "No One Fights Alone". Origin: Created by LSU coach Beth Torina and MSU coach Samantha Ricketts, approved in 2019. The Teal Tradition: SEC softball teams wear teal, the color representing ovarian cancer awareness, during a designated weekend. Impact: The initiative has expanded beyond the SEC to include other universities, growing annually to support cancer education and support. About Alex Wilcox: A Mississippi State freshman (2018) who continued to play while battling cancer, inspiring the nation. Legacy & Awareness Mississippi State retired her No. 8 jersey, making her the first female student-athlete in school history to receive this honor. The campaign focuses on educating people about the symptoms of ovarian cancer, including bloating, cramping, and back pain. The initiative has been recognized with the SEC Sportsmanship Award.
